description: This topic explains the three organs of the state in Tanzania, the Executive, the Legislature and the Judiciary, their functions, the principle of separation of powers and the system of checks and balances among them.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following are the three organs of the state?

options.text: The President, the police and the army
The Executive, the Legislature and the Judiciary
The Cabinet, the courts and the civil service
The ruling party, the opposition and the voters

mcq.explanation: A modern state has three main organs: the Executive, the Legislature and the Judiciary, each with its own duties.

mcq.questionText: Which organ of the state is responsible for implementing laws and government policies?
mcq.explanation: The Executive puts laws and policies into action and runs the day-to-day affairs of the government.

mcq.questionText: Who is the head of the Executive in the United Republic of Tanzania?

options.text: The Speaker of the National Assembly

mcq.explanation: The President is the Head of State, Head of Government and Commander-in-Chief, leading the Executive.

mcq.questionText: The law-making organ of the United Republic of Tanzania is known as the:
mcq.explanation: Parliament, called the Bunge in Kiswahili, is the Legislature and its main duty is to make laws.

mcq.questionText: Which organ of the state has the duty of interpreting laws and administering justice?
mcq.explanation: The Judiciary is made up of the courts which interpret laws and settle disputes by administering justice.

mcq.questionText: Which court is the highest court in the United Republic of Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: The Court of Appeal is the highest court in Tanzania and its decisions are final.

mcq.questionText: The principle which divides the powers of government among three separate organs is called:
mcq.explanation: Separation of powers means each organ has its own duties so that no single organ becomes too powerful.

mcq.questionText: The head of the National Assembly business who presides over its sittings is the:
mcq.explanation: The Speaker presides over the sittings of the National Assembly and keeps order during debates.

mcq.questionText: Which one of the following is a function of the Legislature?
mcq.explanation: Parliament approves the government budget, makes laws and checks the work of the Executive.

mcq.questionText: Who assists the President in running the government and leads government business in Parliament?
mcq.explanation: The Prime Minister leads government activities in Parliament and assists the President in supervising the Executive.

mcq.questionText: The group of ministers appointed by the President to head various ministries is called the:
mcq.explanation: The Cabinet is made up of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and ministers who advise the President and run ministries.

mcq.questionText: Members of the National Assembly who are directly elected by the people in their areas are known as:
mcq.explanation: Constituency members are elected directly by voters in their constituencies during the general election.

mcq.questionText: Why is independence of the Judiciary important in Tanzania?

options.text: So that judges can make laws for the country
So that courts can decide cases fairly without interference
So that the President can control all court decisions
So that the courts can collect taxes

mcq.explanation: An independent Judiciary can judge cases justly without pressure from the Executive or any other group.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a subordinate (lower) court in Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: Primary courts, district courts and courts of a resident magistrate are subordinate courts below the High Court.

mcq.questionText: The system by which each organ of state limits the powers of the others is called:
mcq.explanation: Checks and balances allow each organ to watch over the others so that no organ misuses its power.

fib.questionText: The three organs of the state are the Executive, the Legislature and the _____.
fib.explanation: The Judiciary is the third organ and is responsible for interpreting laws and administering justice.

fib.questionText: The organ of state that makes laws is the _____.
fib.explanation: The Legislature, known in Tanzania as Parliament or Bunge, has the main duty of making laws.

fib.questionText: In Tanzania, Parliament is known in Kiswahili as the _____.
fib.explanation: Bunge is the Kiswahili name for Parliament, the law-making organ of the United Republic of Tanzania.

fib.questionText: The _____ is the Head of State and head of the Executive in Tanzania.
fib.explanation: The President leads the Executive and is also Head of Government and Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces.

fib.questionText: The highest court in the United Republic of Tanzania is the _____.
fib.explanation: The Court of Appeal stands at the top of the court hierarchy and its decisions are final.

fib.questionText: The principle of dividing government powers among three organs is known as separation of _____.
fib.explanation: Separation of powers ensures each organ performs its own duties so that power is not concentrated in one place.

fib.questionText: The officer who presides over the sittings of the National Assembly is the _____.
fib.explanation: The Speaker chairs the National Assembly, guides debates and keeps order among members.

fib.questionText: The group of ministers appointed by the President to run ministries is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The Cabinet, or Baraza la Mawaziri, advises the President and supervises the work of the ministries.

fib.questionText: The body of government employees who carry out government work in the ministries and departments is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The civil service is made up of permanent government workers who put policies and laws into practice.

fib.questionText: The system in which each organ of state limits and watches over the others is called checks and _____.
fib.explanation: Checks and balances prevent any one organ from misusing its powers over the others.

tf.questionText: The Executive is responsible for implementing laws and government policies.
tf.explanation: The Executive carries out laws and policies and manages the daily running of the government.

tf.questionText: The main duty of the Legislature is to interpret laws in court.
tf.explanation: Interpreting laws is the duty of the Judiciary; the Legislature makes laws.

tf.questionText: The President of the United Republic of Tanzania is the head of the Executive.
tf.explanation: The President leads the Executive and is also Head of State and Head of Government.

tf.questionText: The Court of Appeal is the lowest court in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: The Court of Appeal is the highest court; the primary court is among the lowest.

tf.questionText: Separation of powers helps to prevent the misuse of power by any one organ of state.
tf.explanation: By giving each organ its own duties, separation of powers stops power from being concentrated in one organ.

tf.questionText: Parliament has the power to approve the national budget.
tf.explanation: Approving the government budget is one of the key functions of the Legislature.

tf.questionText: The Prime Minister leads government business in Parliament and assists the President.
tf.explanation: The Prime Minister supervises government activities in Parliament and helps the President run the Executive.

tf.questionText: An independent Judiciary means judges decide cases according to the wishes of the President.
tf.explanation: Independence of the Judiciary means judges decide cases fairly according to the law, without interference.

tf.questionText: All members of the National Assembly are appointed by the President.
tf.explanation: Most members are elected by the people; only a small number are nominated, plus special seats and ex-officio members.

tf.questionText: Through checks and balances, Parliament can question and supervise the work of the Executive.
tf.explanation: Checks and balances allow Parliament to ask questions and oversee the Executive so that it does not misuse power.

summary.questionText: Name the three organs of the state.
summary.correctAnswer: The Executive, the Legislature and the Judiciary.
summary.explanation: These three organs share the powers of government, each with its own duties.

summary.questionText: State the main function of the Executive.
summary.correctAnswer: To implement laws and government policies and run daily government affairs.
summary.explanation: The Executive puts laws and policies into action through the President, Cabinet and civil service.

summary.questionText: State the main function of the Legislature.
summary.correctAnswer: To make laws, approve the budget and check the work of the Executive.
summary.explanation: Parliament (Bunge) is the law-making organ and also oversees government spending and work.

summary.questionText: State the main function of the Judiciary.
summary.correctAnswer: To interpret laws and administer justice by deciding cases.
summary.explanation: The courts settle disputes and ensure justice according to the law.

summary.questionText: Mention the main parts that make up the Executive in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Cabinet (ministers) and the civil service.
summary.explanation: These leaders and workers together carry out laws and policies.

summary.questionText: List the main courts in the hierarchy of courts in Tanzania from highest to lowest.
summary.correctAnswer: Court of Appeal, High Court, and subordinate courts (resident magistrate, district and primary courts).
summary.explanation: This hierarchy shows how cases can be appealed from lower to higher courts.

summary.questionText: What is meant by separation of powers?
summary.correctAnswer: It is dividing the powers of government among the three organs so each has its own duties.
summary.explanation: Separation of powers prevents one organ from holding all the power.

summary.questionText: What is meant by checks and balances?
summary.correctAnswer: It is a system where each organ limits and supervises the others to prevent misuse of power.
summary.explanation: Checks and balances keep the three organs accountable to one another.

summary.questionText: Why is independence of the Judiciary important?
summary.correctAnswer: So that courts can decide cases fairly and justly without interference from other organs.
summary.explanation: Independence protects justice and the rights of citizens.

summary.questionText: Give two reasons why separating the powers of the state is important.
summary.correctAnswer: It prevents misuse of power and protects the rights and freedoms of citizens; it also promotes good governance and accountability.
summary.explanation: Separating powers limits dictatorship and helps each organ work responsibly.

hoq.questionText: A minister in the Cabinet refuses to follow a decision made by Parliament about how money should be spent. Which principle of governance is most directly being challenged?

options.text: The Legislature's power to control government spending
The right of citizens to vote

hoq.explanation: Parliament approves and controls the budget, so ignoring its spending decisions challenges the Legislature's power over the Executive.

hoq.questionText: If the Executive could appoint and remove judges at any time without rules, which value would be most weakened?

options.text: The duty of Parliament to make laws
The civil service's duty to keep records
The President's power to sign treaties

hoq.explanation: If the Executive fully controlled judges, courts could not judge fairly, so judicial independence would be destroyed.

hoq.questionText: Why does the system of checks and balances help to protect democracy and the rights of citizens?

options.text: Because it allows one organ to control all the others
Because it removes the need for elections
Because each organ can limit the others, preventing any one from misusing power
Because it gives all power to the President for quick decisions

hoq.explanation: When organs watch over and limit one another, no single organ can abuse power, which protects democracy and citizens' rights.
